Pressure washing Missouri City TX homes, old and new

Missouri City was incorporated in 1956 and had 74,259 residents at the 2020 census, most of them in Fort Bend County with a small part in Harris County. Its housing falls into two broad eras. Quail Valley grew up around a country club and golf course starting in 1969, with most building done by the end of the 1970s. Sienna, a master-planned community of roughly 10,000 acres near the Brazos River, sold its first homes in 1996.

Both get the same humid Gulf air and the same summer storms, but the surfaces differ. Fifty-year-old brick, wood trim and settled walks want a softer approach than a new slab and fresh fence. Telling the company which part of town you are in is a quick way to set expectations.

Drought stages and pavement washing

Missouri City treats Brazos River water at its own surface water plant, built in 2012 and expanded in 2020, and the Fort Bend Subsidence District limits how much groundwater the area can pump. When supplies get tight, the city's 2025 Drought Contingency Plan tightens outdoor use in steps.

Missouri City drought stages that affect outdoor washing
StageOutdoor wateringWashing pavement or gutters
Stage 29 p.m. to 5 a.m. on assigned daysCheck the plan for current rules
Stage 39 p.m. to 5 a.m. on assigned daysProhibited
Stage 4All non-essential use bannedProhibited

Siding, fences and roofs are a separate question from pavement, so if a stage is declared, ask the company what it can still do and what should wait.

Mildew on walls is the exact issue the city's code page names. Soft washing removes it from brick and siding without driving water behind them.

Fence cleaning

City code expects fences kept in good repair, and Sienna's own common-area upkeep includes cleaning and sealing wood fences.

Deck and patio cleaning

Back patios and pool decks on golf course and wooded lots stay damp in shade and get slick with algae.

If a code notice is already on your door

Start by reading exactly which surface the notice names: a wall, a fence, a walk or the driveway. Note any deadline it gives. When you call the line, mention the notice and the date, because that helps the company you are connected with judge how soon it can fit you in and which surfaces to price first. After the work, keep the invoice with the date and the surfaces listed on it. If the city or your association follows up, that piece of paper answers the question quickly. If the notice is about a broken fence board or a leaning section, that is a repair, so you may need a fence contractor as well as a cleaning.

Storm history near the Brazos

During Hurricane Harvey in 2017, the Brazos River rose to record levels and Fort Bend County ordered mandatory evacuations in areas near the river, including what was then Sienna Plantation. Tornadoes on August 26 damaged homes in Sienna and a shopping plaza on Texas Parkway. Homes that took water or debris may still show silt or staining low on fences and walls. A wash after repairs are complete is often the step that makes a property look settled again.

Rinse water and the city's storm drains

Missouri City runs a stormwater hotline for reporting illegal dumping and illicit discharges as part of its storm sewer permit program. Soap, grime and oil rinsed into the street end up in that system. Before work starts, ask how the company keeps runoff out of the inlet and protects your beds and lawn.

Common questions

Can Missouri City code enforcement cite me for mildew on my house?

The city's Code Enforcement page lists mildew among its common code concerns and says exterior surfaces should be kept clean and sanitary. Fences and other accessory structures also need to be kept in good repair. Reported concerns are investigated, so if you get a notice, cleaning the surface and keeping a dated invoice is the straightforward fix.

Is driveway washing banned in Missouri City during a drought?

Under the city's 2025 Drought Contingency Plan, using water to wash pavement or gutters is prohibited in Stages 3 and 4. In Stage 2, outdoor watering is limited to assigned days overnight. Check the city's current stage before you book a driveway or sidewalk job.

My Sienna HOA sent a letter about my fence. What should I ask for?

Ask for a gentle cleaning that removes the mildew and graying without furring the boards, and ask whether the company also stains or seals if your association wants a uniform look. Keep the letter handy when you call so you can describe exactly what it mentions.

Are older Quail Valley homes harder to pressure wash?

Not harder, but they need more care. Most were built in the 1970s, so mortar, trim paint and caulk may be decades old. Ask for soft washing on brick and painted surfaces and low pressure around windows.
